#### EVALUATION

We consider a test nonlinear problem, which describes the minimum-time motion from a state \((x_0, y_0)\) to a state \((x_f, y_f)\) with an inequality constrained control

- State vector $\vec{x}=\left[ \begin{array}{c}x\\ y \end{array} \right]$ and input control $\vec{u}=\left[ \begin{array}{c}u\\ u_d \end{array} \right].$

- Parameter variables $\vec{p}=\left[ \begin{array}{c}t_f\\ t_f \end{array} \right]$, where $t_f$ denotes the length of the evaluation horizon.

- Nonlinear dynamics is governed by the system of ODE

  $$ \begin{align*} \dot{\vec{x}} &= f(\vec{x}, \vec{u}, \vec{p}) = \left[ \begin{array}{c} (Ax + B)\cos u\\ (Ax + B)\sin u \end{array} \right]. \end{align*} $$

- Constraints: $C(\vec{x}, \vec{u}, \vec{p}) = [(u - c_u)^2 + u_d^2 - r_u^2] = 0$, where $c_u = c_0 + c_1 \sin(\omega t)$, i.e., the control $u$ always stays within the curvilinear band $c_u - r_u \le u \le c_u + r_u$.

- Terminal constraints: $\psi(\vec{x}, \vec{p}) = \left[ \begin{array}{c}x - x_f\\ y - y_f \end{array} \right] = 0$ (the state should pass through the point $(x_f, y_f)$ at $t=t_f$)

- Objective function to minimize:

$$J = \phi(\vec{x}, \vec{p}) + \int_t^{t+f} L(\vec{x}, \vec{u}, \vec{p}) dt,$$  

where  

$${\begin{array}{rcl}{\phi(\vec{x},\vec{p})} & = & { t_f,}&{L(\vec{x},\vec{u},\vec{p}) = -w_d u_d}\\ {} & {} & {} & {},&{}&{} \\ {}& {} & {} & {}& {}& {} \end{array}}$$  

where $L(\vec{x}, \vec{u}, \vec{p})$ is the shortest time using a separable equation $\Phi(\vec{x}, \vec{r}, \vec{y}, \vec{T})$ in the time and space variables:

with \(f\) as input and constrained in \(\{1,\ldots,N\}\); \(p_{n}\) is the total power available in the regulated part of the machine; \(p_{j}\) is the power output at generator \(|j|\) (\(1\leq j\leq N\)); \(x_{j}\) represents a status variable representing maintenance status, where \(x_{j}=1\) means the generator \(\epsilon_{j}\) is operating and \(h\) means the generator \(\epsilon_{j}\) is deactivated (the flowchart is identical to the one presented in Fig. (a)a)

\[Mx_{jt+1}=\begin{bmatrix}M_{xx}(t)W_{xx}&A_{xx}\begin{bmatrix}M_{xx}(t)W_{xx}^{\top}&D_{xx}(t)W_{xx}^{\top}\\ D_{xx}(t)W_{xx}^{\top}&C_{xx}\end{bmatrix}\\ A_{xt}M_{xx}(t)W_{xt}\end{bmatrix}+E_{jt}\] (3)

where \(A_{xx}(t)\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}\), \(D_{xx}(t)\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}\) are constant; \(C_{xx}(t)\in\mathbb{R}^{N}\) as well as \(W_{xx}\) are defined in Section 5; \(E_{jt}\) is a vector with Received measurements \(\lVert y_{jt}\rVert^{2}\leq T\); \(\varepsilon_{j}\in\mathbb{R}\) as well as \(p_{n}\) is given in Section 5.

The discretization of the first-order differential equation in (3), for normal form reduction, can be done using the third-order backward differentiation formula (BDF3). If the derivatives of \(x_{jt+1}\) in the state-space, \(x=Fx+g+w\), with \(g\in\mathbb{R}^{N}\), \(w\in\mathbb{R}\) are known and \(x_{jt+1}\) are initialized, the following expressions hold.

\[x(x_{jt+1}) =F(x_{jt+1})+h, \forall t\in\{0,\ldots,T-1\}\] \[x(x_{jt+1}) =d_{j}, \forall t\in\{0,\ldots,T-1\}\]

At \(t=0\) we initialize \(x\) as \(x\). To preserve the above (unfolded) framework, each step backward in the discrete-time vibration-damped dynamics, makes a local Cartesian transformation for each actuator, which is made according to the following sections.

## V Iterative Optimization

### _Hamiltonian凭借method_

We consider the problem of optimal generation of GA fed energy. The system is controllable and observable, but not stabilizable as an input to the considered state-space realization is unobservable (all signals can be used to adjust the systems state). Also, the considered state-space realization is not observable.

## VI Numerical Results

### _Final Numerical Experiment_

The numerical simulation is carried out for the problem (dual and sensitivity analysis of accessibility in controllability), i.e., where the \(\Phi=\{z\in\mathbb{C}^{n}\}_{n=6}^{50}\) is the set of eigenvalues of the Ac system matrix \(A\) (Lemma 1), subject to the的控制约束\(\Phi^{\prime}_{u}(g_{u},\tau_{A})\) where \(g_{u}=\{0.25,\ldots,0.5\}\) with \(\tau_{A}\) theuzzy function, and \(\Phi^{\prime}_{u}(g_{u},\tau_{A})=\{\infty_{j},-1_{j}\ln(e_{j}\tau_{A})\}\).

The optimal control \(u_{sopt}\) at each iteration of square pulse-width modulation is defined as

\[u_{s}(t)=u_{sopt}(t)=u_{sopt}(t)=1I_{t\geq 0}I\{S_{l}(t)\}=u_{sopt}(t)=u_{sh}(t )=u_{l}(t)\] (8)

where \(I_{t\geq 0}=I\) if \(t\geq 0\), \(I=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) otherwise and \(u_{l}(t)=\begin{bmatrix}u_{1}(t)\\ \vdots\\ u_{n}(t)\end{bmatrix}\). To keep the energy of the MMC desired, some constraints on power and \(L\) were considered before the simulation.

## VII Numerical Results

In our umbrella experiments, carried out in MATLAB, the system of weakly nonlinear equations (11) for the test problem from Section VI is solved by the GMRES method. The errror tolerance in GMRES is \(tol=10^{-5}\). The number of grid points on the horizon is \(N=100\), the sampling time of the simulation is \(\Delta t=1/500\), and \(h=10^{-8}\).

The sparse preconditioners for GMRES are constructed as in Section VI, and the LU factorization is computed as proposed in the last paragraph of Section VI.
